statement: A positive locally finite, lattice-rotation/reflection invariant punctured triangular reciprocal-torus measure with a uniform small-annulus mass bound and positive periodized-Cauchy representations modulo arbitrary finite signed errors in all three row charts has a full unique scaling limit c*|p|^(-2)dp. Its scalar coefficient formula includes a finite exceptional-line counterterm. Exact mixtures are the special case E=0, where that counterterm vanishes.
hypotheses: C is positive and locally finite away from the omitted physical origin.
C has all triangular-lattice rotations and reflections.
C{r<=|p|<=2r}<=K for all sufficiently small r>0.
Each rectangular two-sheet projection satisfies C'=integral Q_s dnu + E on k!=0.
nu is positive and finite on horizontal bands away from zero; s ranges over [0,infinity], including Q_0=Dirac(0) and Q_infinity=uniform.
Each E extends to a finite signed measure on the rectangle; atoms and singular errors are allowed.

conclusion.scaling: C_delta is the image near the physical origin under p -> p/delta, without amplitude renormalization.
conclusion.limit: c*|p|^(-2)dp on the whole punctured plane
conclusion.coefficient: c=-2*(L+B_0)/pi, 0<=c<=K/(2*pi*log(2)); B_0=integral_{k=0} Q(p) C(dp) is finite and is zero for exact mixtures.

infinite_scale_obligations: Exceptional physical lines have finite mass controlled by rotated errors and vanish under scaling; exact mixtures remove them and the alias atom outright.
The fourth harmonic and negative cap prove summability of the nonnegative dispersion defect before a limiting argument.
Horizontal bands and rotated normal density bounds give the exact endcap estimate, or its finite-error version.
Summable defect forces limiting mixtures onto s=|k|, and two independent local distributional derivatives fix the inverse-Laplacian form including exceptional lines.
A full scalar cutoff limit exists before extraction; the finite exceptional-line counterterm and endcaps with punctured error corridors control the noncompact tail and determine one coefficient.

jacobian.analytic_applicability: Only factors the harmonic numerator; no installed operation discovered for the infinite-scale measure implication.

extension_example.finite_error: F(dp)=1_{1/4<|p|<1/3}dp in the physical origin chart
extension_example.strict_weakening_reason: The finite perturbation creates an upward normal-density jump that no exact positive periodized-Cauchy mixture can have.

necessary_line_correction.measure: Six equal atoms at R_{pi/3}^j*(0,1/8), j=0,...,5, with a radial Q equal to one there.
necessary_line_correction.cutoffs: Q is radial and equals one on |p|<=1/8; q has the manuscript cutoff properties. At h=1/32 the radial ratio is 4 and each nonzero horizontal ratio has absolute value 2*sqrt(3), all outside q's support.
necessary_line_correction.meaning: Exact counterexample to extending the uncorrected scalar formula to arbitrary finite spectral errors; the original exact-mixture theorem has no such line mass.

independent_review.scope: Analytic proof, source fidelity, and publication-level novelty/significance of the finite-error theorem.
